conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode; sides field states mirrored/same

candidates.name: MovingAverageGapBarGeneral
candidates.quote: if the high of a bar is below the moving average, then there is a gap between that bar and the moving average.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: in a bull trend or sideways market, the bar's entire range sits below the EMA (no overlap). Same test as chapter 13's R13-02, redefined here without any 20-bar no-touch precondition.

complexity.reason: a single EMA value compared against the bar's high; no window loop or persistent state

notes: Identical primitive to R13-02; expected to merge in dedup.

candidates.name: FirstMovingAverageGapBarSwingEntry
candidates.quote: if there is a strong bull and it finally has a bar that has a high below the moving average and then the next bar trades above the high of that bar, the market will try to form a higher high or lower high test of the bull's extreme.
candidates.description: In a strong trend, the first gap bar (R14-01) since the trend began sets up a swing buy one tick above its high, targeting a test of the trend's prior extreme.
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the gap bar's high, held for a swing target near the trend's prior extreme

complexity.reason: needs 'first since trend start' bookkeeping plus a trend-strength read (the AlwaysInDirection family) before the gap-bar test is trustworthy

notes: Same underlying gap-bar-breakout mechanism as R13-03, without the 20-bar no-touch precondition.

candidates.name: SecondAttemptGapBarEntry
candidates.quote: If the market again goes above the high of a prior bar, this is a second moving average gap bar setup, or a second attempt to fill a moving average gap in a bull trend, and the odds are excellent that there will be a tradable rally off this setup.
candidates.description: If a first gap-bar attempt does not hold and the pullback continues, the next bar whose high exceeds the prior bar's high while still below the EMA is a higher-confidence second entry.
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the second gap bar's high

complexity.reason: a persistent attempt counter incremented on each failed first attempt

notes: Same structure as R13-04; this file's version has no 20-gap-bar precondition.

candidates.name: ScalpVsSwingStrengthFilter
candidates.quote: So if there is a strong trend, a first moving average gap tends to set up swing trades, and if there is not a strong trend and a trader takes a moving average gap bar trade, she is more likely looking for a scalp.
candidates.description: Classify a gap-bar entry's intended objective (swing toward the trend extreme vs. a scalp back to the EMA) based on whether the trend is strong.
candidates.pseudocode: strongTrend() -> targetMode = SWING (trend extreme); else targetMode = SCALP (moving average)

complexity.reason: 'strong trend' is a design decision left to the AlwaysInDirection / trend-strength primitives defined elsewhere

candidates.name: InsufficientRoomToEmaFilter
candidates.quote: A trader will take the trade only if there is enough room to the moving average to make an acceptable profit
candidates.description: Block a scalp-style gap-bar fade if the distance from the current close to the EMA is below a minimum tick threshold.

complexity.reason: a single EMA distance compared against a fixed tick threshold

notes: Brooks gives no numeric minimum; minScalpTicks is a reading of 'enough room ... to make an acceptable profit.'

candidates.name: GapAfterStrongTrendTestOfExtremeTarget
candidates.quote: This pullback to the gap bar is typically strong enough to break the trend line and after the test of the trend's extreme, the market will generally form a two-legged correction or even a major trend reversal.
candidates.description: After a first-gap-bar swing entry triggers, target a test of the trend's prior extreme, then expect at least a two-legged correction (take partial profits / tighten stops around the extreme rather than holding for more).
candidates.book_order_type: profit-taking near the trend's prior extreme

complexity.reason: needs the trend's prior extreme (a remembered swing level) plus the leg-counting concept for the follow-on correction

notes: The two-legged-correction/reversal expectation overlaps chapter 16 and 17's leg-counting material; this candidate only captures the target, not the correction shape.

rejected.quote: Some traders will scale into additional longs if the pullback below the moving average falls some more (this is discussed in Chapter 31 on scaling into and out of trades).
rejected.reason: position-sizing/scaling decision explicitly deferred by the book to a later chapter, not a single bar-level condition

rejected.quote: Most bars on most charts are moving average gap bars because most bars do not touch the moving average.
rejected.reason: descriptive statistical observation about bar frequency, not itself a tradable if/then condition

chapter_summary: Generalizes chapter 13's moving-average gap bar beyond the 20-gap-bar precondition: any bar whose range sits entirely on the far side of the EMA is a gap bar, and the first (then second) subsequent break above/below it is a fade toward the trend's extreme (swing trade in a strong trend, scalp back to the EMA otherwise). Produces the reusable gap-bar primitive (R14-01, identical to R13-02), first/second entries mirroring chapter 13's counting structure, a research-grade swing-vs-scalp trend-strength filter, a simple minimum-room-to-target filter, and a hard target/exit candidate for the trend-extreme test. Two passages (scaling into positions, a base-rate observation) are rejected as non-mechanical.
